learnerSteps.instruction: Explain the studied Canadian rights and legal/civic responsibilities, distinguishing general protections from citizenship/age-specific federal voting and legal obligations from voluntary contribution. Use the actual completed collective-action case and create the original shared-goal campaign plan; rights are not rewards for volunteering.

Demonstrate the whole bounded Canadian institutional repertoire: federal/provincial/territorial/municipal and school-board roles, actual current First Nation/Métis/Inuit structures and their supported functions, and distinct contributions to studied shared service/social and environmental cases. Retain the complete prior Ontario municipal/FN/Métis governance checks; neither generic people identity nor a single service example substitutes for them.

Describe the actual contrasting input methods and why governments at all levels need suitable opportunities to hear affected people. Separately recognise the supplied Crown-action/rights/possible-impact conditions for the constitutional consultation duty and appropriate accommodation; a public survey, meeting count, automatic approval or universal veto is not an equivalent explanation.

Explain how supported differing experiences and priorities can shape views of the selected issue or response without assuming either a whole people’s opinion or that honest disagreement is lying. Connect actual named governments/actions to the issue and assess what the source supports rather than invent complete effectiveness.

Use a changed original service/development issue with its authority and relevant rights facts supplied. Identify distinct government, departmental, representative/advisory and citizen roles; choose a suitable public-input/civic method; explain whether the separate consultation conditions may matter; and identify missing facts instead of assigning every power to the nearest body. Retain each whole contributing claim and source-specific performance check, not only a combined label-matching exercise.

citizens-and-government.positive: Explains the relevant citizen rights/roles and actual different government structures/responsibilities, shared work, participation and distinct consultation duty, then applies them with source and authority limits.
